_meta.purpose: The three registries every item-partition author validates against: the rarity ladder, the equip roles/frames, and the top-level item category taxonomy. Consumed by ~125 parallel authoring agents.
_meta.immutability: FROZEN v1 once an owner flips `frozen` to true and authoring begins against it. A rung, role, or category id and its ordinal/position are never renumbered or reused after that point. Any later change is v2, minted only after an explicit owner re-run decision — never an in-place edit of this file.
_meta.appendOnlyRule: Ordinals (rarity) and list positions (roles, categories) are append-only. A new rung/role/category is added at a free ordinal or at the end of its list; an existing one is never renumbered, and a retired one is marked disabled in its own downstream table, never deleted from here.
_meta.idGrammarNote: All ids in this file are lowercase-kebab. Downstream authors: `container_id` (seed-contract.md §4) allows NO DOT in its body — separate segments with hyphens, never dots.

rarity.appendOnly: rarity_id values and their ordinal are append-only. Ordinals are pre-spaced by 10 precisely so a future rung can be inserted (e.g. at 15 or 85) without renumbering any existing rung.
rarity.axisNote: Rarity controls count band and tier window only. It never touches a magnitude — that is item level's job, and item-ideal's own boundary (ssot-rarity.md §3.2, §3.6).

ladder.name: Chaff
ladder.flavor: husks, clippings, a dented bucket. Salvage fodder.
ladder.note: the only rung with no pool — base type plus implicit only.

ladder.name: Sprout
ladder.flavor: it works. That is all it does.

ladder.name: Cultivated
ladder.flavor: grown on purpose, to a plan.

ladder.name: Fused
ladder.flavor: two natures in one object — the game's own word.

ladder.name: Chimeric
ladder.flavor: the fusion went further than intended.

ladder.name: Heirloom
ladder.flavor: a line kept alive longer than its keepers.
ladder.note: pity-guarded rung (bad-luck protection may key on this ordinal).

ladder.name: Firstseed
ladder.note: promotion ceiling — this is the highest rung an item may be promoted into.

ladder.name: Sunwoven
ladder.flavor: made of sun, not of matter.
ladder.note: pity-guarded rung; drop-only, never reached by promotion.

ladder.name: Almanac
ladder.flavor: it has a page. Everyone knows its name.
ladder.note: top rung; deliberately unguarded by pity, but must have at least one deterministic (quest/boss) source.

roles.appendOnly: roleId values and their list position are append-only.

frames.meaning: a human-like body. Carries the full 15 roles. Frame is not faction (a humanoid body can be plant- or zombie-side).
a plant-like body — rooted, handless. Carries the full 15 roles under a parallel, botanically-grounded vocabulary. Frame is not faction.

a chimera body combining both natures. Carries 13 of the 15 roles (drops ward-array and jewel-minor-b); each remaining role accepts a base type from either pure frame's ladder. The commander never wears this frame — it takes humanoid or plant only.

list.hybridDropReason: a chimera body has no single coherent outer layer to shed as a sheath; its shield families migrate to core-guard at a reduced tier cap instead.
a second graft onto a body that is already two natures does not take.

commanderOnly.note: one slot, not several. Binds at match owner-scope so its atoms reach the whole squad. Priced from a separate 100‰ commander budget, never drawn from the body's 1000‰.

categories.appendOnly: category ids and their list position are append-only.

list.bindsTo: player, with the instance binding to an actor at equip
player, with its effect targeting an actor at use
list.authorNowNote: Authored at Diablo-2 scale (owner decision 2026-08-22). The consumable lane ships a degenerate use path — spent at a menu before a run, effect lasts the run — with the effect authored as real atoms from day one, so the action layer absorbs it later without a migration. Fleet plan stage 1b carries 3 consumable partitions.

list.bindsTo: player, binding into an item rather than an actor
list.authorNowNote: Authored at Diablo-2 scale (owner decision 2026-08-22), overruling the content-budget recommendation to ship sockets at zero. Fleet plan stage 1a carries 3 gem partitions and stage 1b one socket-word partition.

list.bindsTo: player, with the bonus binding at player-scope
list.store: instance if rolled, stack if not
list.authorNowNote: Authored at Diablo-2 scale (owner decision 2026-08-22), overruling the content-budget recommendation to ship charms at zero. Fleet plan stage 1b carries 3 charm partitions. Note the charm lane's own finding: no runtime today both binds a charm correctly and executes it, so charm rows are content-complete and consumer-pending.

elements._note: Added wave 0b: element is a VALIDATED field in seed-contract 2.1 but no item registry owned the vocabulary, so the validator was deriving it from themes elementAffinity. Sourced from ElementRoster / element-hub-ssot.md. Six concrete elements plus omni. Ordinals are load-bearing in the shipped code — append-only, never reorder.

omni.note: Additive-only. Not part of the matchup ring; it is the untyped slot every generated element family also emits.

elements.matchupNote: The ring plus a light/dark mutual counter. Two matrices exist and are asymmetric — the shield matrix is not the combat ring. Item content names an element; it never encodes a matchup.

powerCategories._note: The five power-vector categories. Added wave 0c: entry-shapes.md found that charm axes and socket resonances key on this vocabulary and no registry owned it. Distinct from tags.v1.json combat-posture, which is a coarse three-value tagging axis for filters and vendor stock, not the power vector.
consumers: the power vector itself, when E9 ships

counterPressure._note: Added wave 0c. ssot-uniques.md requires every unique to carry a drawback, a condition, or deliberate narrowness, and the validator rejects one that does not. But only "narrow" was expressible without a number: "drawback" wanted a negative magnitude and "conditional" wanted a threshold, both banned by seed-contract §3. These closed vocabularies make all three authorable numberlessly.

kinds.meaning: the item is strong in a deliberately small slice of situations. Needs no further field.
the item is worse at something. Requires severityBand and a channel or family reference.
the item is only strong while a named condition holds. Requires condition.

conditions._note: Closed list. A condition an author needs that is absent is a BLOCKED report, never an invented string. Each maps to a predicate-tree leaf the atom layer already ships, so none of these is a promise the runtime cannot keep.

frozenNote: FROZEN v1. Consumed by the wave-1 authoring fleet. No in-place edit from here: a required change is registryVersion 2 plus an explicit decision on which partitions re-run. A silently edited registry splits the corpus into pre-edit and post-edit semantics that nothing downstream can tell apart.
minCompatibleNote: v1 is current; no breaking change yet.
stage1aFrozen: Stage 1a authored and validated at 0 errors (205 entries, 25 files). From here a change to this registry invalidates authored content unless minCompatibleVersion says otherwise.
